text: Two genuinely basic things to check before you go diagnosing anything more complicated at all: is the gateway itself actually running an up-to-date version, and does the report even have a gateway selected in the first place.

Every single refresh attempt, whether it succeeded or genuinely failed, gets logged right here — its status, its duration, and any specific error message it produced along the way. This refresh history is where any real refresh problem should always start getting diagnosed.

One rule genuinely worth memorizing for good: four consecutive failures in a row, and Power BI automatically disables the entire schedule on its own, with no extra warning beyond the failure emails themselves landing in your inbox.

Common causes worth recognizing on sight: Gateway Not Reachable almost always means an outdated gateway version needing an update. A processing error with a type mismatch usually points to a problem in your Power Query script, or an outdated Desktop version. And a refresh that times out often means the semantic model has simply grown too large or complex for shared capacity's two-hour processing limit.

If you're receiving failure emails you genuinely no longer want, an admin can remove your address from that specific semantic model's own notification settings directly — this is an admin action taken on the model itself, not a setting inside your personal email client. And that genuinely closes out Chapter Ten completely. Chapter Eleven shifts the whole conversation from keeping data current to controlling exactly who gets to see which specific rows of it — Row-Level Security, starting with the very next lesson.
